body:
## What it does:
* When reopening a file, this will make sure the cursor is placed back to the position where you left before.
* This implements `:help restore-cursor` in a nicer way.
* Creates autocommand for |BufReadPre| and |FileType| event with |MiniMisc.restore_cursor|

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

This is still work in progress. However I wanted to ask if you would be fine integrating this.

This is debatable. In my mind, this functionality serves two purposes:
- Reduce friction for user to move cursor to its latest place - cursor is already there.
- Reduce friction for user to search visually for cursor - it is in the center of screen and outside of folds.

The second point is not valid under current implementation. I would get it if it would require more work/code to achieve "always centered" behavior, but it is the opposite.

comment_data.body:
Let's follow this as general design:
- `setup_restore_cursor()`:
    - Receives `opts` with at least two possible fields `ignore_buftype` and `ignore_filetype`. Their defaults are as in example (not empty). Use the following approach:
     ```lua
    if not H.is_array_of(x, H.is_string) then
      H.error('In `setup_restore_cursor()` `opts.x` should be an array of strings.')
    end
    ``` 
    - Validates `opts` and ensures defaults are in place.
    - Creates Neovim<0.7 compatible autocommand following `:h restore-cursor`. I think something like this should work:
    ```lua
    local au_command = string.format(
      [[augroup MiniMiscRestoreCursor
          au!
          au BufRead * au FileType <buffer> ++once lua MiniMisc.restore_cursor(%s)
        augroup END]],
      vim.inspect(opts)
    )
    vim.api.nvim_exec(au_command, false)
    ```
- `restore_cursor()`:
    - Also takes `opts` as described earlier, but doesn't validate it.
    - Makes all necessary checks that prohibit restoring cursor.
    - Restores cursor with `vim.cmd([[normal! g'"zvzz]])`.

+MiniMisc.setup_restore_cursor = function(opts)
